title: Synthetic cargo adaptors reveal molecular features that enhance dynein activation

key_results: Engineered adaptors outperform endogenous adaptors in generating highly motile transport complexes; adaptor identity modulates dynein velocity and cellular trafficking behavior

title: Prenatal PM2.5 exposure drives epigenetic reprogramming of fetal macrophages linked to atopic dermatitis
task: Link prenatal PM2.5 exposure to atopic dermatitis through epigenetic reprogramming of fetal macrophages
key_results: First-trimester PM2.5 exposure associated with increased childhood AD risk; FCER1G hypomethylation in fetal macrophages caused sustained overexpression persisting to AD-affected skin and immune cells; FCER1G networks promote NADPH oxidase ROS and Th2 pathways
comments: The multi-omics integration and single-cell resolution strengthen causality inference, but direct in vivo functional validation of FCER1G-mediated AD pathogenesis is lacking.

model_io.model: placental and fetal tissue from PM2.5-exposed pregnancies
single-cell RNA-seq and integrative multi-omics of fetal macrophages, AD skin macrophages

hypotheses.result: FCER1G hypomethylation detected in fetal macrophages; transcriptional program persists across development and re-emerges in AD skin

title: Macrophages tune NK cell IFNγ production through direct lipid transfer
task: Elucidate macrophage-mediated suppression of NK cell IFNγ production through lipid transfer
key_results: LPS-stimulated macrophages transfer fatty acids to NK cells via trogocytosis-mediated CD36 transfer, suppressing mTORC1 and IFNγ by ~60% (lipid accumulation-dependent); blocking macrophage fatty acid synthesis restores NK function
comments: The identification of trogocytosis as the transfer mechanism is novel, though the direct quantification of IFNγ suppression magnitude would strengthen the claims.

model_io.model: primary macrophage-NK cell co-culture in vitro and in vivo

hypotheses.hypothesis: Macrophage-derived fatty acids directly suppress NK cell mTORC1 and IFNγ production
hypotheses.result: Lipid accumulation in NK cells correlated with mTORC1 suppression and reduced IFNγ; blocking macrophage fatty acid synthesis prevented lipid transfer and restored both parameters

hypotheses.hypothesis: CD36 trogocytosis mediates fatty acid transfer from macrophages to NK cells
hypotheses.result: CD36 protein transfer via trogocytosis associated with fatty acid accumulation in NK cells; genetic knockdown blocked transfer

hypotheses.hypothesis: OHB-Ffar3 signaling downregulates Hopx, disrupting ACTC1-mediated contractility

title: Breathing ferroelectricity, flat-bands and multiple chiral phonons in van der Waals breathing kagome Nb3Cl8
task: Investigation of breathing ferroelectricity, flat-bands, and chiral phonons in van der Waals Nb₃Cl₈
key_results: Breathing ferroelectricity from breathing-in/out distortion of Kagome triangles; exciton-like absorption peaks (thin layers) vs. semiconductor edge (thick layers) from flat-bands and interlayer interaction; multiple chiral phonons and temperature-induced electronic/magnetic transitions
comments: Comprehensive experimental validation of theory predictions; multiferroic properties and flat-bands make this a rich platform but device integration challenges remain.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed; energies match theoretical calculations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temperature-induced transitions correlate with electronic-phase and magnetic changes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; phonon and flat-band temperature dependencies consistent

title: Design and analysis of a slotted square 1 × 2 MIMO terahertz patch antenna with machine-learning-based gain prediction and equivalent rlc validation
task: Machine-learning gain prediction for graphene-based THz MIMO antenna with equivalent circuit validation
key_results: Slotted square 1×2 MIMO antenna: 3 resonant modes at 4.63, 5.34, 6.15 THz (BW ~0.5 THz each); max gain 14.6 dB, efficiency 92%, mutual coupling -33.03 dB, ECC 0.0001, DG 10 dB; XGBoost gain prediction: MAE 3.79%, R² 91.77%
comments: Multiband MIMO design is comprehensive; XGBoost ML model shows strong predictive power but generalization to other substrates/geometries untested.

title: Development of (polyvinyl alcohol/O-carboxymethyl chitosan/PbO) nanocomposites for efficient gamma radiation protection

key_results: Linear and mass attenuation coefficients (μ, μ/ρ) measured across 59.53-1332 keV; HVL, TVL, MFP calculated; experimental μ matches XCOM predictions; PbO nanoparticles produce uniform compact films; effective radiation protection demonstrated
comments: Comprehensive characterization (SEM, TEM, EDX, XRD, TGA, DSC) validates material synthesis; noted degradation concern limits long-term applicability despite promising shielding efficiency.

title: Equivalence analysis of thermal response of materials irradiated with constant power and ultra-long pulsed laser

key_results: Peak temperatures from constant power and ultra-long pulsed laser are approximately equivalent; time to reach maximum temperature deviates <17%; validated on thermally-thick material
comments: Simple and practical equivalence framework; validation limited to one material—generalization across thermal conductivities and ablation thresholds requires broader experiments.

title: Influence of cross-sectional geometry on the wave attenuation performance of floating breakwaters: an experimental study
task: Experimental investigation of floating breakwater geometry effects on wave attenuation
key_results: Rectangular FBW: 47% baseline attenuation; triangular (30°): 66% efficiency (+19% vs. rectangular, 56% less material); trapezoidal: 83% peak efficiency; leeward-oriented slope outperforms seaward; upright orientation superior to inverted
comments: Systematic geometric optimization is practical; trapezoidal profile with leeward slope recommended balances performance, stability, and constructability—valuable for coastal engineering.

title: A unified framework for non-Hermitian localization with boundary-insensitive modes and electric-magnetic analogy
task: Unified theory of non-Hermitian localization with boundary-insensitive skin effects
key_results: Spatially inhomogeneous imaginary potentials produce boundary-insensitive skin effect; classification into electric (scalar) and magnetic (vector) types with phase transition to full delocalization
comments: Novel insight that boundary-insensitivity arises from translational symmetry breaking; practical control via potential engineering is significant but requires experimental validation in photonic/cold-atom platforms.

title: A universal Fano type scattering model and its experimental tests

comments: Elegantly explains Fano asymmetry through constructive/destructive interference; generality across transmission and notch geometries strengthens the framework.
